findings.finding: Trial-local PTRA/QROT contribution scratch can be initialized from an F-KT checkpoint, accumulated without mutating committed crop state, discarded on rejected trials, and admitted only with a post-commit certificate. This supplies the crop-side semantics but does not own the physical commit point.

The runtime captures the checkpoint, executes the physical trial, rejects incomplete mass or invalid candidates, and calls fmr_commit_candidate. Therefore the actual decision point that publishes physical state is inside F-MR runtime execution.

A successful kernel_commit_candidate is the authoritative atomic physical-state publication: candidate state is moved into committed state, revision increments exactly by one, committed time becomes candidate origin_t1, and the candidate is cleared. Failed commits leave committed state unchanged.

The exact QROT-equivalent rate is sum(root_extraction_sink) of the preformed root sink physically supplied to the Richards trial. No additional dz factor is admissible. Recomputing uptake after the trial would not prove identity with the physically applied sink.

Restricted PTRA production is separately qualified, but current canonical serialized MultiSWAP runtime does not carry that PTRA quantity together with the same checkpoint/trial provenance and commit decision.

No existing generic commit observer, accepted-side-effect, callback or sidecar seam was found on the current composed source lineage that can atomically associate trial-local process metadata with successful F-KT publication.

atomicity_analysis.reason: If physical F-KT commit succeeds and a subsequently called fallible WOFOST window-admission routine returns a normal runtime error, physical committed state and accepted-window metadata can diverge. The outer WOFOST owner cannot roll back an already published F-KT revision.
atomicity_analysis.reason_precommit: F-WOF34 semantics intentionally require proof of an actual F-KT commit. Admitting before commit would allow a later commit rejection to contribute crop integrals from a non-accepted physical trial.
atomicity_analysis.required_resolution: A generic F-MR/F-KT-adjacent commit-associated observer or accepted-side-effect seam must own the composition point. It must prevalidate all expected failure modes before physical publication and ensure that the post-publication metadata action is total/non-fallible for the prevalidated payload, or otherwise make physical publication and side-effect publication one recoverable transaction under the same owner.

required_properties_of_owner_seam: does not move F-KT commit authority into crop code
same checkpoint lineage/revision/interval as the physical candidate
zero contribution on routing, solver, temporal, mass, candidate or commit rejection
accepted contribution exactly once after successful commit
prevalidation before commit of any condition that can produce an expected runtime rejection
post-commit path must not expose a normal recoverable error that leaves side-effect metadata missing
inactive columns incur no persistent optional-state allocation
no solver scratch added to column state
mass accounting and applied Richards sink remain unchanged
generic time only, no calendar assumption

owner_handoff.suggested_title: Generic Commit-Associated Accepted Side-Effect / Observer Seam
owner_handoff.resume_condition: F-MR owner qualifies a generic transaction-safe commit-associated seam on the composed postimage.
